name: EBITDA_L3_growth_return_neighbors
mechanism: Within an industry, EV/EBITDA is roughly a function of expected growth and the return earned on reinvestment (value driver formula: multiple rises with growth when ROIC exceeds the cost of capital). Selecting same-industry peers that are closest in recent growth and ROIC should match the fundamentals that the industry median averages away.
prediction: Median |ln error| below the 0.333 industry-median baseline in at least 3 of 4 exploration years, with pooled median around 0.31.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

name: EBITDA_L2_risk_growth_harmonic
mechanism: EV/EBITDA reflects growth, profitability of growth and risk; leverage (net debt/EBITDA) and size proxy for risk and cost of capital. Using a broader 2-digit pool gives more candidates so the distance ranking can find close fundamental matches, and the harmonic mean limits the upward bias from high-multiple outliers.
prediction: Beats the industry median (0.333) and the Bhojraj-Lee warranted multiple (0.357) on pooled median error, and has a lower mean error than 0.513.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, ebitda_margin 0.5, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback []

name: EBITDA_L4_size_peers
mechanism: Firms in the same narrow 4-digit SIC line share product markets, cyclicality and technology, and close size matches share scale-related risk and liquidity premia. This is a refined version of the traditional analyst comp set, falling back to coarser industries only when the narrow set is too thin.
prediction: Pooled median error within 0.02 of the industry-median baseline or better, beating it in at least 2 of 4 years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l4 | rank log_sales 1, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=6, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2]

name: Sales_L2_margin_matched
mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so differences in margin dominate cross-sectional EV/Sales dispersion. Matching peers on EBITDA and gross margin within the same broad industry, plus growth, should remove most of the margin-driven error that plagues industry-median EV/Sales.
prediction: Pooled median error well below the 0.603 industry-median baseline (target under 0.50), beating it in all 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

name: Sales_crossindustry_fundamental_twins
mechanism: Valuation per dollar of sales is determined by how much of that sale becomes cash flow (margin), how fast it grows and capital needs (asset turnover); these economics can be matched across industry boundaries. Dropping the industry screen enlarges the pool so very close margin-growth twins can be found, with the harmonic mean controlling outlier peers.
prediction: Beats the industry median EV/Sales (0.603) and the Bhojraj-Lee warranted multiple (0.674) on pooled median error in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/Sales | rank ebitda_margin 2, sales_growth_1y 1, asset_turnover 0.5, gross_margin 0.5 | k=15, harmonic_mean, min_peers=3

name: Sales_L2_margin_band_growth
mechanism: A hard band on EBITDA margin guarantees that peers convert sales into cash flow at a similar rate, which is the first-order determinant of EV/Sales; within that band, matching growth and returns captures the remaining value drivers. Industry membership adds shared risk and cyclicality.
prediction: Pooled median error below 0.55 and below the industry-median EV/Sales baseline in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [same industry_l2]

name: EBITDA_industry_fundamental_neighbors
mechanism: Within a 3-digit industry, EV/EBITDA differences are driven mainly by expected growth, profitability persistence and size-related risk. Choosing the industry peers closest in sales growth, EBITDA margin and scale should isolate firms with similar discount rates and growth paths, removing the noise from dissimilar members of the same industry.
prediction: Median |ln(V_est/V)| below the L3/L2 industry median baseline (0.333) in at least 3 of 4 exploration years, and pooled median at or below 0.32.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1.5, ebitda_margin 1, log_sales 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

name: EBITDA_reinvestment_adjusted
mechanism: EBITDA ignores the capital needed to sustain it, so firms with heavy capex convert less EBITDA into free cash flow and deserve lower EV/EBITDA. Matching on capex intensity and return on capital, alongside growth, within a broad 2-digit industry pairs firms whose EBITDA has similar cash-flow value per dollar.
prediction: Beats the L3/L2 industry median baseline in at least 3 of 4 years; improvement concentrated in capital-intensive 2-digit sectors.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank capex_intensity 1.5, roic 1, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

name: EBITDA_narrow_industry_harmonic
mechanism: The finest industry definition shares the most similar business models, cost structures and investor clienteles, so its members should trade at similar EBITDA multiples. The harmonic mean is the theoretically consistent average for price-scaled ratios and damps the influence of peers with inflated multiples from temporarily depressed EBITDA.
prediction: Median error within 0.02 of or below the industry median baseline (0.333), and a lower mean error than that baseline (below 0.513) in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l4 | k=all, harmonic_mean, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2]

name: Sales_margin_matched_industry
mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so a firm's sales multiple is driven chiefly by how much profit each dollar of sales generates. Ranking 2-digit industry peers mainly on EBITDA margin, then growth and size, should remove the largest source of dispersion in sales multiples.
prediction: Median error below 0.50 pooled, beating the L3/L2 industry median baseline (0.603) in all 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 3, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

name: Sales_cross_industry_margin_band
mechanism: Because margin and growth explain most of the variation in EV/Sales, firms with near-identical economics can be good comparables even across industries. A band on EBITDA margin followed by ranking on margin, gross margin, growth and size builds a peer group of economic twins without relying on SIC codes, which are coarse for diversified firms.
prediction: Beats the industry median EV/Sales baseline (0.603) in at least 3 of 4 years, with pooled median error below 0.55.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=15, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.1] -> []

name: Sales_industry_profitability_efficiency
mechanism: Within a 3-digit industry, firms with higher gross and EBITDA margins and lower asset intensity earn more value per dollar of sales. Matching on margins and asset turnover captures both pricing power and capital requirements, which together determine how much enterprise value a dollar of revenue supports.
prediction: Beats the industry median EV/Sales baseline (0.603) in at least 3 of 4 years and beats the Bhojraj-Lee warranted multiple (0.674) in all 4.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, asset_turnover 1, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

name: Sales_L2_margin_growth
mechanism: EV/Sales factors into EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so differences in profitability dominate differences in sales multiples, and growth adds to value per dollar of sales. Within a 2-digit industry, peers matched mainly on EBITDA margin, then on gross margin and growth, should share the target's value per dollar of sales.
prediction: Pooled median |ln error| below 0.55, beating the L3/L2 industry median (0.603) in all 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

name: EBITDA_L3_growth_reinvestment
mechanism: Under a DCF, EV/EBITDA is driven by expected growth, by how much of EBITDA must be reinvested (capex) and by the return on that reinvestment. Same-industry peers share risk and accounting conventions, and ranking within the industry on growth, capex intensity and ROIC picks the peers whose cash-conversion and growth profile match the target's.
prediction: Median |ln error| below the L3/L2 industry median (0.333) when pooled over FY2016-2019, and lower than the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, capex_intensity 1, roic 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

name: EBITDA_L2_quality_leverage
mechanism: A wider 2-digit industry pool gives enough candidates to match on drivers: margin quality and growth set the expected path of EBITDA, net leverage proxies financial risk, and size proxies diversification and liquidity. Firms alike on all four should be priced at similar EBITDA multiples.
prediction: Pooled median |ln error| at or below 0.33 and below the Bhojraj-Lee warranted-multiple peers (0.380) in every exploration year.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, ebitda_margin 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

name: EBITDA_L3_size_capex_harmonic
mechanism: The harmonic mean of multiples equals the ratio of aggregate value to aggregate EBITDA, so it is not pulled up by peers with temporarily low EBITDA, which is the main source of upward bias in EBITDA multiples. Matching peers within the 3-digit industry on size and capital intensity aligns scale economies and maintenance-capex burden.
prediction: Pooled mean |ln error| below the industry-median baseline mean (0.513), with median |ln error| within 0.02 of 0.333 or better.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank log_sales 1, capex_intensity 1 | k=12, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

name: Sales_crossindustry_margin_band
mechanism: Because EV/Sales = EV/EBITDA x EBITDA margin and EV/EBITDA varies far less across industries than margins do, firms with near-identical EBITDA margins and similar growth and reinvestment needs should have similar sales multiples whatever their SIC code. A tight margin band followed by fundamental ranking uses the whole cross-section instead of small industry groups.
prediction: Pooled median |ln error| below the Bhojraj-Lee warranted multiple (0.674) and below the industry median (0.603) in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank ebitda_margin 2, sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 1, capex_intensity 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.1] -> []

name: Sales_L3_margin_size
mechanism: Within a narrow 3-digit industry, business models and cost structures are similar, so what is left of the variation in sales multiples comes mostly from profitability, growth and scale. Ranking close industry peers on EBITDA margin first, then growth and size, should cut the large errors of plain industry medians on EV/Sales.
prediction: Pooled median |ln error| below 0.57 and lower than the industry median (0.603) in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 2, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=6, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

Picking the nearest neighbours on growth, EBITDA margin, leverage and size inside the 2-digit sector holds technology and cyclicality roughly fixed while matching the value drivers that differ across firms in the same sector.

mechanism: In a steady-state DCF, EV/EBITDA rises with expected growth and with the efficiency of reinvestment (ROIC), and falls with capital intensity and financial risk. Within a 3-digit industry, choosing the peers closest on growth, ROIC, capex intensity and leverage matches those value drivers more closely than taking the whole industry.

compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, capex_intensity 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []

name: EBITDA_L2_size_growth_margin_harmonic
mechanism: Larger, faster-growing, higher-margin firms in the same broad sector carry lower risk and more durable cash flows, so they trade at similar EBITDA multiples. The harmonic mean averages earnings yields instead of multiples, so a few richly priced peers have less pull and the upward bias of the arithmetic mean goes away.

mechanism: Valuation theory says the multiple depends on growth, return on capital, reinvestment need and risk, not on the SIC label. Picking peers from all industries on those fundamentals alone tests whether matching fundamentals across industries does as well as the industry screen when an industry has few members or a mixed set of firms.

name: SALES_L2_margin_band
mechanism: EV/Sales is roughly EV/EBITDA times the EBITDA margin, so firms with very different margins cannot share a sales multiple even within one sector. A hard ±10-point EBITDA-margin band inside the 2-digit industry, followed by ranking on margins and growth, removes the biggest source of error in EV/Sales.
prediction: Median error below 0.50 in every exploration year, beating the 0.603 industry-median baseline in 4 of 4 years.

name: SALES_crossindustry_profitability_harmonic
mechanism: A dollar of sales is worth what it turns into as cash flow: profitability (EBITDA and gross margin), growth and capital needs (asset turnover). Matching on these across all industries and taking the harmonic mean of the 20 nearest peers' sales multiples gives a stable, less skewed estimate that leans on economics more than SIC codes.
prediction: Median error below 0.55 pooled and below the Bhojraj-Lee regression (0.674) in all 4 years.

mechanism: Inside a narrow 3-digit industry the business model is broadly shared, so what is left of the variation in sales multiples comes mostly from profitability and growth. Ranking same-industry peers on EBITDA margin, net margin and growth, and keeping a small nearest set, should capture this.
